_comment: Per-machine runner config, keyed by hostname (`socket.gethostname()`).
COMMITTED on purpose: configure a box once and it syncs, instead of being a
setup step that has to be remembered per clone and is silently missing until
something quietly fails to dispatch.
capabilities — the slugs a card's `requires:` is checked against. An
unlisted hostname resolves to nothing, so a card that needs the ComfyUI box
simply does not dispatch on a machine that lacks it, at zero token cost.
Adding a machine is a visible edit here, never an accidental capability.
DECLARED, not probed — and not because detection is hard. It isn't; whether
the graphics model is installed is a few lines of Python. The reason is what
the check is FOR (the origin project's maintainer, 2026-07-23). A probe answers 'is the stack
present?', and the honest response to 'no' from an agent with initiative is
to install it — 20 GB of weights onto the laptop at 3 AM, which no gate
would catch because nothing about it breaks a rule. A declaration answers a
different question, 'is this machine ALLOWED to do this work?', where 'no'
is a decision already made rather than a problem to solve.
permission_mode — handed to `claude --permission-mode`. bypassPermissions is
what a code card needs; the default acceptEdits cannot run Bash, so pytest
and git are unavailable and the card burns an attempt doing nothing. What
contains it: the worker runs in a throwaway worktree outside the repo, on
its own branch, and the runner refuses to build on dev/main/master. What it
does not contain: it is the whole machine, not a sandbox.
allowed_tools — optional, only meaningful below bypassPermissions. A tool
the card needs but the list omits is DENIED, and in -p mode there is nobody
to ask, so the worker stalls and the attempt is spent for a reason that
looks nothing like the real one. Tighter, but it trades one risk for a
subtler one.
`.ai/host.json` (gitignored) overrides this file wholesale, for a one-off
answer on one box that you do not want to commit.
